cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Lose Something for Me
cards.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a rosette on like yours. You're dressed for my opening night already; come with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine says FINALIST. I'm dressed for the awards dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, a finalist in my audience. Come to the play instead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: If I'm not there, the prize goes to the runner-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them you're coming to my play. I want to hear you choose it over the prize.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a rosette as readiness for A's play; B2 reveals finalist status and A3 keeps the confident invitation while making B sacrifice that honor.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 finalist fact feeds A3 finalist-in-audience pressure; B4 forfeiture causes A5 request to choose the play over the prize aloud.

relationship.evidence: B2 has an awards commitment and B4 a stated penalty, a credible personal reason to resist.

heightening.evidence: A5 asks for an overt communicated choice after B4 makes the loss explicit.

specificity.evidence: A1 opening night and B2 award dinner plus B4 runner-up clarify the alternative rewards.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 tell them and hear you choose are aimed at a real loyalty demonstration, not a hidden explanatory narrator.
